transcript: I can build something with AI now, get it looking pretty polished, and start thinking, I could sell this. But I can get that far before I know why someone would choose it over what they're already using. I've got other things I want to build too. So I want more to go on before I give this one more time. So I'm building what I call a GTM engine to help me figure that out. It looks at the code behind what I've built, then researches who might need it and what they're using already. That helps me work out what to test. I'd still want to let someone try what I've built on something they actually need to do and see whether they choose it over their usual way. Maybe I've got to build a bit more to find that out. That's fine. I don't have to decide it's a business just to keep working on it. And if I just enjoy using it myself, I can leave it at that. It's okay to have a hobby. So you guys tell me, what made you decide to turn something you'd built into a business?
engine: faster-whisper small.en; beam5; VAD; no previous-text conditioning; no initial prompt
normalization: Punctuation/case/apostrophe style; spelled AI/GTM; gotta/got to and wanna/want to only. No omission or paraphrase allowance; contractions such as you'd remain required.
